title: Sinoatrial exit block
summary: The sinus node fires on schedule, but one impulse fails to leave it. The pause equals twice the usual interval.

events.label: Regular beats
events.caption: The sinus node fires every 0.8 seconds and each impulse leaves the node to activate the atria.
events.ecg: Normal P waves and QRS complexes.

events.label: Exit block
events.caption: The node fires on schedule, but this impulse cannot leave it and reach the atrial muscle. The sinus node's own firing is too small to see on the ECG.
events.ecg: A beat is missing where one was due.

events.label: Beats resume
events.caption: The next impulse gets out. The pause is exactly twice the usual P-P interval: the node never lost its rhythm, one beat was simply blocked.
events.ecg: The pause is a whole multiple of the P-P interval (type II).

teaching_points: Sinoatrial exit block: the sinus node fires but some impulses do not exit to the atria.
Type II: the pause is a multiple of the P-P interval. Type I (classic grouped beating) shows progressively shorter P-P intervals before a pause.
Unlike a sinus pause, the underlying node rhythm keeps its timing.
